stories.body: Captain Smit Machchhar, an Indian pilot recovering in Abu Dhabi, said he fought to reopen the cockpit door after allegedly being stabbed by his co-pilot during a Flydubai flight from Dubai to Tel Aviv. The Boeing 737, carrying about 182 people, descended sharply before passengers and crew restrained the alleged attacker and two reserve pilots aboard landed it safely in Tabuk, Saudi Arabia. Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said the Omani co-pilot appeared to have tried to crash the aircraft, while the UAE is investigating whether terrorism was involved. Machchhar told Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi that, despite his injuries, he knew he could not let the passengers die.
stories.headline: Flydubai captain recounts fighting off alleged cockpit attack to prevent a crash

stories.body: The United States is sending the USS Theodore Roosevelt carrier strike group and a Marine expeditionary unit carrying more than 2,000 Marines toward the Middle East, according to a US official cited by Al Jazeera. The deployments could add 9,000 to 10,000 personnel and would leave three US aircraft carriers and two amphibious groups near Iran by late November. The buildup comes as the Iran war enters its eighth month, with a tanker reported hit in the Strait of Hormuz and Yemen government forces reporting strikes on Houthi targets. US officials say the deployment is intended to preserve military options regardless of diplomatic developments.
stories.headline: US military buildup raises fears of escalation in the Iran war as tanker is hit in Strait of Hormuz

stories.body: Washington has urged European allies to release strategic diesel reserves immediately to ease prices elevated by the US war on Iran, while President Donald Trump has suggested he could restrict US diesel exports. European governments are discussing a coordinated response, and the UK says it is not facing a supply shortage despite relying on the United States for roughly 30% of its diesel imports. UK diesel prices passed £2 a litre for the first time, according to the RAC, as the government emphasized its 42 days of reserve supplies and sought talks with European partners.
stories.headline: US pressure on Europe to release diesel reserves follows fuel-price surge and possible export ban

stories.body: Ethiopia and Eritrea have cut diplomatic relations after Addis Ababa said it would close its embassy in Asmara and expelled 10 Eritrean diplomats on national-security grounds. Eritrea called the allegations of hostile activity unfounded and responded by severing ties. The rupture coincides with expanding conflict between Ethiopian federal forces and an alliance involving the Tigray People's Liberation Front and other armed groups across Tigray, Amhara and Afar. Ethiopia has accused Eritrea, Sudan and Egypt of backing the opposition alliance, allegations they deny, while communications blackouts and fighting around key transport routes are limiting independent reporting.
stories.headline: Ethiopia and Eritrea sever diplomatic ties as fighting in northern Ethiopia expands

stories.body: Russian drones struck Kyiv's Southern Bridge for the fourth time in 24 hours, forcing its closure and disrupting a key crossing in the Ukrainian capital. The attack is part of an intensified Russian campaign against Kyiv and Ukraine's energy system ahead of winter. Ukraine says Russia suffered record monthly casualties in September while its forces retook territory around Lyman, though casualty and territorial claims from either side cannot be independently verified. Recent Russian strikes have also hit power infrastructure, residential buildings, schools and other civilian sites, causing deaths and outages.
stories.headline: Russia again strikes Kyiv's Southern Bridge as attacks on the Ukrainian capital continue

stories.body: More than half of Europe experienced very strong heat stress this summer, while western Europe recorded its hottest summer on record, according to the EU's Copernicus climate monitor. Western European temperatures from June through August were 2.5C above the recent decadal average, and Europe as a whole had its third-warmest summer. The report linked recurring heatwaves, drought, fires, low river flows and pressure on energy, transport and health systems to a warming climate, with heat contributing to tens of thousands of excess deaths and damage to harvests.
stories.headline: Europe records widespread heat stress after a summer of heatwaves and excess deaths

stories.body: Tennessee death-row prisoner Christa Pike remains in critical condition in hospital after surviving two doses of pentobarbital during an attempted execution, her lawyers said. Her legal team described repeated unsuccessful attempts to establish an IV line and said observers were left without information after a curtain was closed while Pike was still breathing. Governor Bill Lee has halted executions for the rest of the year and ordered an independent review, while Pike's lawyers seek commutation of her sentence and consider further legal action. Pike was sentenced to death in 1996 for the murder of Colleen Slemmer.
stories.headline: Christa Pike remains in critical condition after surviving failed lethal-injection execution in Tennessee

stories.body: New York Governor Kathy Hochul has appointed Attorney General Letitia James as special prosecutor in an investigation into allegations that a Cornell University student was drugged and raped by several fraternity members in 2024. Hochul said she no longer had confidence in the local district attorney's ability to oversee the case fairly. The accuser, identified in court filings as Jane Doe, has filed a civil lawsuit alleging that Cornell failed to protect her and inadequately disciplined those involved. Cornell supports presenting the matter to a grand jury, denies failing to punish those responsible and has agreed to an independent review.
stories.headline: New York appoints Attorney General Letitia James as special prosecutor in Cornell fraternity rape case

stories.body: The Supreme Court has agreed to review Immigration and Customs Enforcement's mandatory-detention policy for immigrants, in one of the first cases accepted after the Court's summer recess. The case is expected to be among the most consequential matters of the term beginning next week, with the ruling likely to shape how broadly the federal government can hold immigrants in detention while their cases proceed.
stories.headline: Supreme Court agrees to examine ICE's mandatory immigrant-detention policy

stories.body: The Treasury Department has issued long-awaited rules for the nation's first federal school-voucher program, increasing pressure on Democratic governors to decide whether their states will participate. The regulations establish the framework for implementing the program, which has been closely watched by public-school advocates, school-choice supporters and state officials.
stories.headline: Treasury issues rules for first federal school-voucher program

stories.body: Junts per Catalunya has confirmed it will oppose two government housing decrees in Congress, making their approval unlikely and putting Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez's minority government under renewed pressure. The government has refused to withdraw or amend the measures, urging Junts to abstain and allow them to proceed as urgent legislation. The standoff follows protests over housing and evictions, including the case of Maricarmen Abascal, and has prompted speculation that Sánchez could call an early general election if the parliamentary coalition cannot be rebuilt.
stories.headline: Junts maintains opposition to Spain's housing decrees, deepening pressure on Sánchez

stories.body: Eastern Spain is facing severe rainfall and flood risks as a Dana weather pattern brings cold upper air over the warm Mediterranean. Forecasts warned that some areas could receive 200 to 300mm of rain, with Valencia and Castelló among the places most at risk. Catalonia placed several towns under lockdown and Valencia closed schools affecting nearly half a million children, while red alerts were issued for intense downpours in parts of Catalonia and the Valencian Community.
stories.headline: Torrential rain triggers flooding alerts, transport disruption and school closures in eastern Spain

stories.body: Spain added 92,327 Social Security contributors in September, its strongest September employment gain since records began, bringing total employment to 22.43 million. The extraordinary regularization of migrants was the main driver: foreign-born workers accounted for about 84,220 of the new affiliations, and more than 421,000 people had entered formal employment through the process by the end of the month. Registered unemployment also rose by 23,587 to 2.37 million, a rise officials described as partly administrative as newly regularized workers register before finding work.
stories.headline: Spain's September employment rises by 92,000, aided by migrant regularization

stories.body: Morocco has made no official public response to plans for King Felipe VI and Queen Letizia to visit Ceuta and Melilla on October 13 and 14, visits expected to carry diplomatic sensitivity. It will be the first visit by a Spanish head of state to the two autonomous North African cities in 20 years. Spanish officials expect some form of Moroccan protest closer to the trip but do not expect bilateral relations to break down, despite lingering tension following the recent mass crossing into Ceuta.
stories.headline: Morocco stays silent over King Felipe VI's planned visits to Ceuta and Melilla

stories.body: A housing protest encampment in Barcelona's Plaça de Catalunya expanded from about 50 tents to around 200 after the Sindicat de Llogateres joined, with the city council estimating that roughly 450 people were participating. Protesters are mobilizing against Junts per Catalunya's planned vote against the national housing decrees and have called for further demonstrations, including one outside the party's Barcelona headquarters. Dozens gathered there on Friday, temporarily blocking part of Carrer de la Marina, before organizers directed participants toward an attempted eviction blockade in the Raval.
stories.headline: Barcelona's housing encampment grows as protesters press Junts to back national housing decrees

stories.body: Heavy storms in southern Catalonia have flooded parts of the Terres de l'Ebre, disrupted rail traffic and prompted school closures across affected municipalities. Emergency authorities warned that rainfall could reach 200mm in places, with red-level risk for intense rain in the Baix Ebre, Montsià and nearby areas. Trains were halted between Tarragona and Ulldecona, while numerous roads were closed, including a 20-kilometre stretch of the N-340 between Alcanar and Amposta. Civil Protection activated the INUNCAT emergency plan and advised residents to avoid travel and low-lying areas near rivers and ravines.
stories.headline: Flooding in the Terres de l'Ebre disrupts rail service and leads to school suspensions
